items.title: PAX Aus 2026 Guest Lineup Includes Former WWE superstar Austin Creed, Doom Composer Mick Gordon, and More
items.description: The only thing they fear is you. And Mick Gordon’s guitar, probably.
items.author: Luke Reilly
items.content:
PAX Aus has revealed an eclectic lineup of gaming and gaming-adjacent guests will be on deck for PAX Aus 2026 this October.

Leading the list is Austin Creed, formerly known to wrestling aficionados by his WWE superstar Ring name Xavier Woods. A lifelong gamer, Creed is the host of popular gaming YouTube channel UpUpDownDown.

Also appearing will be award-winning Australian composer and sound designer Mick Gordon, whose incredible work on the likes of 2016’s Doom and the follow-up Doom Eternal – as well as the much-loved MachineGames Wolfenstein series – has earned him enormous praise. Gordon will be taking fans on a tour behind some of this music.

Housemarque’s Gregory Louden will also be at PAX Aus 2026, fresh off his work directing PlayStation-published Saros. Born and raised in Sydney, Louden is currently based in Finland at Housemarque, where he now serves as creative director.

You can browse a full list of the guests announced today on the PAX Aus website, or below.

Today’s guests join the previously-announced Storytime speaker, Holly Longdale, on the 2026 bill. Longdale is executive producer of World of Warcraft.

“PAX Aus has always been about bringing together incredible people from every corner of gaming and gaming culture,” said PAX Aus event director Lauren Luciani in a statement provided alongside today’s announcement. “This year’s guests represent the breadth of the community we celebrate, from game development and content creation to tabletop gaming, fantasy literature, voice acting, and live performance. We’re thrilled to welcome them to Melbourne and can’t wait for fans to experience everything they have to share.”

PAX Aus 2026 will take place at the Melbourne Convention and Exhibition Centre from October 9-11, and will once again conclude Melbourne International Games Week.

Luke is a Senior Editor on the IGN reviews team. You can track him down on Bluesky @mrlukereilly to ask him things about stuff.

items.title: Wreckreation 2 Announced Despite Studio Closure, Just Nine Months After the Original Arrived
items.description: Former Burnout boss Fiona Sperry has established a new studio to develop the sequel.
items.author: Luke Reilly
items.content:
Former head of Burnout developer Criterion Games Fiona Sperry is doubling down on 2025’s Wreckreation by announcing a sequel is on the way. The news may come as unexpected, considering the lukewarm response to the original, and the fact that the entire team at developer Three Fields Entertainment was placed on notice of redundancy in the immediate wake of Wreckreation’s release, with no further support from publisher THQ Nordic forthcoming.

Wreckreation 2 is technically being developed by a new studio called When Tides Turn, although this studio is reportedly staffed by veterans of Three Fields Entertainment. Prior to Wreckreation, UK-based Three Fields Entertainment made Dangerous Golf, plus the Burnout-adjacent racers Danger Zone and Dangerous Driving.

Coming to PC, PS5, and Xbox Series X|S , Wreckreation 2 has no precise release date yet – but has only been in development for about three months, according to Rock Paper Shotgun.

Wreckreation 2 is described as more compact than the original, trading its predecessor's enormous yet bland and one-note rural map for something that contains a lot more urban environments. The result seems to be something that may be even closer in spirit to the likes of Burnout Paradise than the original Wreckreation, which already explicitly recreated modes, sound effects, and parts of Burnout Paradise’s on-screen presentation.

IGN’s November 2025 review of Wreckreation noted its “unpredictable handling, dull open-world map, [and] samey event structure” made it tough to recommend, and that it “feels like a supermarket brand homage to a series of better arcade racers, built with the user-generated content tools of another game.”

Luke is a Senior Editor on the IGN reviews team. You can track him down on Bluesky @mrlukereilly to ask him things about stuff.

items.title: Former Tekken Director Katsuhiro Harada Reveals He Totally Misunderstood What Getting Invited To the Cookout Meant After Fans Loved the Leroy Smith Reveal
items.description: Katsuhiro Harada, former director of the Tekken series, opened up about a hilarious misunderstanding he had with his international fans after revealing Leroy Smith for Tekken 7.
items.author: Virginia Glaze
items.content:
Katsuhiro Harada, former director of the Tekken series, opened up about a hilarious misunderstanding he had with his international fans after revealing Leroy Smith for Tekken 7.

Leroy Smith is genuinely one of the coolest characters to ever join the Tekken universe. The Wing Chun practitioner was an instant hit when he was first revealed in Tekken 7, even inspiring cosplays from celebrities like T-Pain.

In fact, the ‘Grandmaster of Drip’ was so well-received that Black American fans started ‘inviting Harada to the cookout,’ leaving the Japanese game director extremely confused.

Harada opened up about the humorous exchange in response to a fan on X, who shared a clip from 1985 cult classic The Last Dragon, arguing that Tekken must’ve been inspired by the martial arts movie and Black culture.

In his reply, Harada revealed that after Leroy was announced in 2019, he received a message from the American fan community: “Can we invite you to the cookout for making an awesome character like this?”

“Now, as someone from my generation in Japan, I was actually considered relatively good at reading and writing English. By then I’d already been to North America over 50 times, had maintained the English I learned for university entrance exams, and had been communicating with people on Twitter in English long before translation apps became useful, let alone AI translation,” he prefaced.

“But honestly… When I saw that sentence, I had absolutely no idea what it meant. In fact, my very first reaction was: ‘Oh no… I’m finished.’”

Harada explained that, at the time, he’d been seeing the word ‘cooked’ a lot online, as well as reading articles that were “spreading hate toward video games.” Having learned to associate the word “cooked” with terms like “destroyed,” he was under the impression that fans hated Leroy.

“For one terrifying moment, I read it as: ‘Hey… we… we… can invite you to a party where we’re going to beat you up and roast you?’” he continued. “Even though I thought I knew America pretty well, I genuinely wondered if I’d somehow pressed some invisible cultural button that I wasn’t supposed to touch.”

Luckily, someone eventually explained the concept of getting invited to the cookout. Harada explained that it was like receiving “one of the highest compliments possible — basically saying, ‘You’re someone we’d trust enough to invite to our close-knit family BBQ, where only real friends and loved ones are welcome.’

“That explanation was a huge relief,” he continued. “Then they started showing me BBQ equipment and ingredients, and I was absolutely shocked that everything was several times bigger than what we have in Japan. Sure, I expected the smoker grills to be huge. But even the tongs and spatulas were enormous, and the meat looked like something I’d only ever seen as loot in an MMORPG.

“Looking back now, I honestly regret not immediately flying to the U.S. and accepting an invitation to one of those community cookouts. That really was the perfect opportunity.”

For me, this is already a story from a career that spans the past 31 years.

I’m probably one of the people in the game industry who has traveled to the largest number of countries and actually met local fan communities in person. So honestly, I’ve been influenced by people and… https://t.co/0gcUeWB8ds pic.twitter.com/or7szlYKhZ

— Katsuhiro Harada (@Harada_TEKKEN) July 20, 2026

To end his humorous anecdote, Harada confirmed that he was greatly influenced by several prominent Black figures, specifically citing Michael Jackson, Wesley Snipes as Blade, Kareem Abdul-Jabbar in Game of Death, and Jim Kelly in Enter the Dragon.

“Of course I can’t claim that I fully understand what you call Black culture. But if we’re talking about the parts that have genuinely influenced me, the cookout story is certainly one of them,” he said.

Harada famously left Bandai Namco and the Tekken franchise earlier this year, choosing to open his own development house, VS Studio, where he hopes to create a new fighting game and return to his roots in game development.

(Photo by SIA KAMBOU/AFP via Getty Images)

items.title: Ed Harris Reveals Dutton Ranch Scene Producers Cut That Made Him Want to Quit the Yellowstone Spinoff
items.description: Ed Harris felt “misled” by his role on Yellowstone spinoff series Dutton Ranch, saying he nearly wanted to void his contract over issues with how his character, Everett McKinney, was used… or rather, how he wasn’t used.
items.author: Virginia Glaze
items.content:
Ed Harris felt “misled” by his role on Yellowstone spinoff series Dutton Ranch, saying he nearly wanted to void his contract over issues with how his character, Everett McKinney, was used… or rather, how he wasn’t used.

Harris opened up about the situation in a carpet interview with Variety at the premier of Apple TV’s ‘The Dink,’ speaking plainly about his difference of opinion with producers at Paramount.

The actor, who portrays grizzled Vietnam veteran Everett McKinney, says he was told that McKinney would be one of four main characters on the Dutton Ranch spinoff. But according to Harris, that didn’t end up holding true.

“Midway through the first season, I was ready to say, ‘Get me the f**k out of here,’ to tell you the truth,” he explained. “I didn’t feel I was being used. I felt very misled. Prior to signing on for it, I was talked to quite a bit about what the season was, and what my character was going to do, and that I was one of the four main characters. And that wasn’t really the case.”

He even approached the producers over this issue, but their conversation didn’t end up really going anywhere. That being said, he’s been told McKinney will have “a little bit more to do” in Season 2. He is currently signed for two seasons of the show.

“I said, ‘I’m feeling underused and inconsequential,’ and they kind of went, ‘Oh,'” he continued. “I was just a little frustrated, to tell you the truth.”

While Harris claimed it was “frustrating” not doing as much as he’d anticipated while actively filming, the result ended up being “pretty good” in his opinion.

“It seemed like I was relatively important to the story, but the doing of it didn’t feel that way,” he said.

However, what really hacked him off was the choice to axe a scene where McKinney got to sing at the local watering hole — something that got under his skin so bad, he considered voiding his contract with the studio.

“The thing that really pissed me off, to tell you the truth, is the first episode I think it was, or the second, one of the things they told me before I signed on was, ‘Hey, you get to sing a song in the bar.’

“I’m talking to [Beth Dutton] at the bar, and [Rip Wheeler] comes in and says, ‘Okay, Everett, come on, it’s your turn,” Harris said. “I walk up to the mic, and they cut it. ...They cut the song out. I’m going, ‘Fuck you, people.’"

Ed Harris says he felt “misled” about his “inconsequential” role on “Dutton Ranch,” and that halfway through filming Season 1, he was telling his team to “get me the f--- out of here.”

“Prior to signing on for it, I was talked to quite a bit about what the season was, and what… pic.twitter.com/StmmazVogC

— Variety (@Variety) July 21, 2026

Producers told Harris it was “too up” for the “dark ending of that episode,” but for him, it was “reason enough to say, ‘I’m voiding my contract.’”

Dutton Ranch Season 1 is available to stream on Paramount+, with Harris confirming that Season 2 is expected to start filming in February 2027.

(Photo by Frazer Harrison/Getty Images)

items.title: New La La Land Poster Finally Fixes Issue That Bothered Ryan Gosling for Years
items.description: An updated version of the La La Land movie poster has finally fixed an issue that’s haunted Ryan Gosling for nearly a decade.
items.author: Virginia Glaze
items.content:
An updated version of the La La Land movie poster has finally fixed an issue that’s haunted Ryan Gosling for nearly a decade.

La La Land is turning ten years old, and to celebrate, Lionsgate has created a new version of the film’s iconic movie poster that shows Gosling and co-star Emma Stone dancing while the lights of Los Angeles watch in the background.

This update comes as a welcome reprieve for Gosling, who has long complained of an issue in the original poster: his left hand. Or, as he calls it, “La La Hand.”

As told by the star himself in a 2024 interview with WSJ, he wasn’t aware the photo would become the flick’s official poster. "We were supposed to have our hands up, and I thought it would be cool to put my hand [more flat], even though everyone told me it wasn’t cool,” he explained. “I was sure it was cooler. Now when I look at it, and I have to see it all the time, you know, what would’ve been cooler… [the intended pose]. It just killed the energy that way.”

La La Land is coming back to theaters starting Sunday, August 16 in honor of its 10th anniversary. Movie-goers can see it in Dolby Cinema at AMC Theaters and relive the musical romantic comedy-drama that won six Oscars and seven Golden Globes, following aspiring actress Mia and jazz musician Seb as they try to carve out their lives in Los Angeles. IGN gave the film a 9.5 out of 10, with Terri Schwartz calling it a “joyous filmgoing experience” and a “musical brimming with optimism that never becomes treacly.”

This isn’t the only big news for La La Land; it’s also getting a Broadway adaptation, which will feature music from Justin Hurwitz and lyrics by Benj Pasek and Justin Paul, all three of whom worked on the soundtrack for the film.

Marc Platt, producer for La la Land, said he was “thrilled” to bring the flick to Broadway, calling it the “next exciting chapter in its evolution.”

“We’ve assembled a world-class team to create a musical that will delight ‘La La Land’s’ millions of current fans and introduce the property to a whole new audience.”

items.title: Ghost in the Shell Fans Can't Decide if the New Prime Video Series Is Better Than the 1995 Movie
items.description: Fans of Masamune Shirow’s Ghost in the Shell manga are at odds with 1995 film adaptation truthers after Science Saru’s 2026 Prime Video anime sparked a heated debate in the community.
items.author: Virginia Glaze
items.content:
Fans of Masamune Shirow’s Ghost in the Shell manga are at odds with 1995 film adaptation truthers after Science Saru’s 2026 Prime Video anime sparked a heated debate in the community.

If you’ve been keeping up with the summer anime season, you’ve probably heard all about the newest Ghost in the Shell adaptation (titled The Ghost in the Shell, to be clear). It’s one of many, and it’s arguably the closest to the source material — but that’s where things get sticky.

The original 1989 manga features a decidedly less gritty artstyle than Mamoru Oshii’s 1995 movie, which, like myself, was many folks’ introduction to the franchise. Oshii’s take on Masamune’s work transformed it from the cartoony, oftentimes slap-stick affair that contrasted heavily (and purposefully) from the high-concept cyberpunk material at its core to a dark, brooding, and haunting tale that left young viewers in a chokehold, setting the tone for the property from then on out.

That’s why, when the first episode of Science Saru’s anime dropped on Prime Video this summer, Ghost in the Shell fans were split; some lauded its faithfulness to Masamune’s original manga, while others were left pining for Oshii’s special sauce that defined the franchise for so long. Those who prefer Stand Alone Complex seem to land somewhere in the middle, though it’s basically agreed upon that SAC is fantastic in its own right.

The central debate here isn’t whether or not Science Saru’s 2026 anime is the definitive take on the manga — that’s indisputably true — but if it’s better than Ghost in the Shell’s very first screen adaptation.

While the answer is completely up for debate and a matter of personal taste, that hasn’t stopped the internet from doing what it does best: arguing. One of the central hubs for this argument has taken place on X/Twitter, where two clips from both the 1995 film and the 2026 series were placed side-by-side, showcasing the difference in style between Production I.G. and Science Saru and how each studio handled telling the same part of Motoko’s story.

Camouflage scene in 'Ghost in the Shell'

1995 vs 2026 pic.twitter.com/9hKxFaG8QJ

— Culture Crave 🍿 (@CultureCrave) July 10, 2026

As you can probably guess, the reactions have been animated, to say the least. “Why's it the old versions are usually better than the new ones?” one viewer wrote, while another remarked that they “love how the new Ghost in the Shell is close to the original manga.”

Yet another posted a GIF from Guardians of the Galaxy showing Starlord telling Drax the Destroyer, “It’s worse. It’s so much worse.”

“The 1995 version is still untouchable,” yet another argued.

It depends on whether or not your idea of “better” is up to art direction or faithfulness to the original material, and begs the question — can adaptations, famous for generally making things worse, actually make them better?

In my opinion, the answer is: sometimes, yes. And in the case of Oshii’s 1995 Ghost in the Shell movie, it certainly did. On top of being first to the finish line, it eschewed the manga’s cartoonish style and bawdy humor in favor of a more realistic art style and darker tone throughout when, combined with its brooding dialogue and chilling music, make it a clear winner on both writing and style points.

An X user named ‘Banksy’ puts it best: “I know this new one is closer to the manga, but the sheer aura of the original movie is unbeaten. Every other adaptation seems worse compared to it.”

But that’s just like, my opinion, man. Let us know how you feel in the comments below, and be sure to check out Prime Video’s Ghost in the Shell series if you haven’t already.

items.title: Metal Gear Solid Creator Hideo Kojima Quips That He Wants to Die in a Movie Theater, Just as the Film Itself Is About to Start
items.description: Veteran game director and self-confessed movie buff Hideo Kojima revealed that he’d like to pass away in a movie theater, just as the film itself is about to start.
items.author: Wesley Yin-Poole
items.content:
Veteran game director and self-confessed movie buff Hideo Kojima revealed that he’d like to pass away in a movie theater, just as the film itself is about to start. The 62-year-old made the comment at a film festival in Rome earlier this month, and recently shared a clip of the moment on his official X account.

“I’ve always thought that when I die, I would like to die in a movie theater,” Kojima said in Japanese, as translated by IGN. He goes on to explain that “I love the bit before the movie starts the most. Enter the movie theater, the lights go off and commercials and trailers play, yeah? I’d like to die just before the movie starts.”

Kojima delivered this declaration in a serious tone but with a hint of a smile. The Metal Gear Solid and Death Stranding creator is, after all, a prolific cinemaphile, proclaiming on his X account profile that 70% of his body is made up of movies.

This isn't the first time Kojima has spoken about his own death. Last year, hot on the heels of revealing a number of discarded video game ideas and even an idea for a ‘Forgetting Game’ where the main character gradually forgets important information and abilities if you take too long a break from playing, Kojima said he had left his staff a USB stick of game ideas for after he dies.

As reported by VGC, Kojima issued the morbid revelation to Edge magazine, and discussed his change of thinking that occurred during the pandemic. “Turning 60 was less of a turning point in my life than my experiences during the pandemic,” he said. “I fell seriously ill at that time, and also had an eye operation. Until then, I didn’t think I was old, you know? I just didn’t feel my age, and I assumed I would be able to create for as long as I live.

“But then I became sick, and I couldn’t create anything. And I saw lots of people around me passing away at that time. I was confronted with death. Of course, I recovered, but now I was thinking, ‘Wait, how many years do I have left to make a game or a film?’ Perhaps I have 10 years?”

Also last year, Kojima discussed his fears as he has got older. "What I am most afraid of is time," he told GQ. "I am afraid of dying and having dementia. I am afraid of forgetting things when I get old. I am afraid that I won't even realise what I am forgetting."

Kojima made this latest quip at the Piccolo America Foundation’s 12th edition of Il Cinema in Piazza, an outdoor film festival in Rome. As reported by Game Surf, he took part in panel discussions and introduced several movies. On July 4, he introduced Shunya Ito’s 1972 film Female Prisoner Scorpion: Jailhouse 41, the second movie in Japanese studio Toei’s exploitation series. The movie and its star, Meiko Kaji, were a big influence on Quentin Tarantino, so much so that Tarantino borrowed Urami Bushi (the theme song sung by Kaji) for the soundtrack to Kill Bill. Kojima noted that the Female Prisoner Scorpion series’ use of inventive cinematography and camera angles, plus the young crew’s commitment to creating something unique on a very limited budget, inspired him as a game creator.

He also introduced Dario Argentino’s Profondo Rosso (1975) on June 5, praising the moment in the movie when both the protagonist and viewer realize the truth at the same moment. “It is something I try to put in my own games as well," Kojima said.

"He also explained that he referenced the gorier moments in Argentino’s films in Policenauts and Snatcher by including decapitation, but that this became a no-go when he moved on to making PlayStation console exclusives.

The final film Kojima presented at the festival alongside Death Stranding 2 actor Luca Marinelli was Sergio Leone’s The Good, the Bad and the Ugly (1966). Kojima said that growing up, his movie-watching family took him to see both American and Italian Westerns, and that he was struck by the sharp difference in their worldview, noting that while the sheriff always wins in American Westerns, Italian Westerns have characters that are much more human and less clear cut. Kojima said that the moral ambiguity of Leone’s Westerns won him over as it reminded him of Akira Kurosawa’s classic films.

Kojima’s movie influences show clearly in his games, stretching back to 1987’s Metal Gear and 1988’s Snatcher. But it was the groundbreaking Metal Gear Solid, which brought cinematic lighting, fully-voiced dialogue, and the series’ famously long movie-like cutscenes to PlayStation gamers all over the world back in 1998. Kojima has previously namechecked war movies like The Great Escape and The Guns of Navarrone as among the influences on MGS, with Snake’s character design riffing off Kurt Russel’s Snake Plisskin in Escape from New York.

With Death Stranding 1 and 2, Kojima managed to bridge the gap between game and movie even more by featuring the fully captured performances of well-known actors like Norman Reedus and Lea Seydoux.

Over on X, Kojima often shares his thoughts on recent movies he’s seen in theaters, as well as Blu-ray releases he has picked up. He seems to watch a broad range of films from various genres, countries and decades. He also popped up on an episode of the Criterion’s closet picks, where he appeared overjoyed to be surrounded by so many movies and enthusiastically introduced his picks.

Kojima is also an avid collector of physical media including vinyl records, CDs, DVDs, and Blu-rays. In the wake of Sony’s recent announcement to stop releasing games on disc, Kojima retweeted a comment on the importance of physical media, warning of the dangers of a digital-only future.

He went further with this train of thought at Il Cinema, specifically calling out Sony: "Since production is ending in 2028, this is about video games, but I grew up with physical media, so I find it really sad," Kojima said. "Currently, I’ve been buying up a lot of Blu-rays, such as various movies, and CDs too."

Hideo Kojima is currently working on experimental horror game OD, which is slated to be published by Xbox Game Studios in collaboration with Get Out director Jordan Peele. At the time of writing, the game doesn’t have a release window yet.

Photo by Rosdiana Ciaravolo/Getty Images.

Verity Townsend is a Japan-based freelance writer who previously served as editor, contributor and translator for the game news site Automaton West. She has also written about Japanese culture and movies for various publications.

items.title: Lara Croft’s Acrobatics Were So Important to Tomb Raider: Legacy of Atlantis That Actress Alix Wilton Regan Started Rock-Climbing to Get Into Character
items.description: The minds at Crystal Dynamics and Flying Wild Hog explained why bringing back Lara Croft’s iconic acrobatics and movement was so important to Tomb Raider: Legacy of Atlantis, and fans couldn’t be happier about it.
items.author: Virginia Glaze
items.content:
In a new episode of their mini-docuseries, the minds at Crystal Dynamics and Flying Wild Hog explained why bringing back Lara Croft’s iconic acrobatics and movement was so important to Tomb Raider: Legacy of Atlantis, and fans couldn’t be happier about it.

Legacy of Atlantis is the latest reimagining of Lara Croft’s debut adventure, marking a stark contrast from the gritty realism of the reboot trilogy.

Amazon Game Studios’ fresh take on the original 1996 Tomb Raider brings back Lara’s high-flying movement, both in traversal and combat. As told by game director Raul Siqueira, “This is a moment where a normal person would step to the side. Lara Croft doesn’t step to the side; she cartwheels to the side, because she’s fast, because she’s agile, because she can do all of those things.”

In a July 21 episode of the game’s behind-the-scenes mini-doc, the team made it clear that they’re bringing back old-school Lara Croft for the new generation — and that includes all of her badass abilities like handstands and swan dives.

“She’s moving confidently, with all these acrobatics, climbing and jumping,” principal technical game designer Grzegorz Grzywacz said. “That’s what makes Lara, Lara.”

“All of those things were the biggest issue for us. Because a regular jump isn’t a Lara Croft regular jump, right?” creative director Michal Kuk added.

In fact, Lara’s physicality was so integral to the game that her actress, Alix Wilton Regan, trained extensively in several different disciplines to get into character.

“I did a lot — I still do a lot — of weight training, running, yoga, rock-climbing. I freakin’ love rock climbing, that is my jam,” she said.

In previous episodes of the docuseries, Regan was shown in full mocap getup, solving ‘puzzles,’ exploring treacherous terrain, and getting into standoffs with as-yet unrevealed enemies on set.

“She is very, very strong. She is very, very capable. …I really wanted to bring that confidence to Lara,” Regan said.

Fans are ecstatic about the developers’ dedication to Lara’s classic moves, which the team confirmed players will be able to practice to their hearts’ content before setting off to explore new areas of the game.

“This is the NUMBER ONE thing for me — I’m so grateful the devs are focusing on Lara’s movement and advertising it as a major factor in defining her,” one player wrote on YouTube.

“Her acrobatics are a part of her character. Literally no one else has or ever done it like her. Thank you for bringing it back to life!” another said.

“I'm so happy the handstand and swan dive are back. Iconic Lara abilities,” yet another praised.

Speaking at IGN Live 2026, Regan said she recorded for three weeks at a time, joking that, “You get a bit hot and sweaty and extremely intimate with your costars doing ten hours in a mocap suit."

IGN got the chance to preview the game at Summer Game Fest 2026, with Simon Cardy saying it "makes a 30-year-old adventure feel brand-new."

Initially slated for a 2026 release, Tomb Raider: Legacy of Atlantis now launches on February 12, 2027, for PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X/S, PC, and Nintendo Switch 2.

items.title: Dbrand's Steam Machine Wraps Are Here
items.author: Wes Davis
items.content:
Just a few weeks after Dbrand revealed its Companion Cube was a lie (or rather that it didn't get permission to make it), the company is back with some new wraps for Valve's little cube-shaped gaming PC. They include nine fun new skins with matching Steam Controller options, among plenty of other options.

The new skins can make your Steam Machine look like a basketball, black or white dice, a brick wall, a dusty old PC, the planet Earth, and a shabby old shipping package. In addition to those, there are also many familiar skin designs that Dbrand has sold for other products over the years, like its groovy inky color blends and circuitry designs, and even a smattering of pastel, one-color options.

Here are some of the new designs:

Finally, some proper Steam Machine wraps! When it comes to Steam Machine accessories, the cosmetic kind have been hard to come by so far. You can find all of these new skins over on Dbrand's website. They come in three tiers. The Essential Kit covers just the faceplate and starts at $17.95; the Deluxe Kit is a full wrap and starts at $34.95; and the Everything Kit includes a controller skin and starts at $44.95.

items.title: A Free Dungeon Crawler Carl Flash Game Is Now Available to Play Online
items.description: Dungeon Crawler Carl just got its first free Flash game that stars none other than Princess Donut.
items.author: Jacob Kienlen
items.content:
The Dungeon Crawler Carl series is having a big year. The live-action TV show was officially confirmed, and there's even a tabletop RPG coming out in December. And while those are the two biggest adaptations coming down the pipeline, there's actually a Dungeon Crawler Carl game that just came out that you can play for free right now.

Mama's Night Off is a Princess Donut-inspired flash game created in collaboration with Maeve Chocolate. The game features a cartoon Princess Donut shooting magic missiles at falling cherries. Each shot is accompanied by an audible "Pew!" voiced by the audiobook narrator Jeff Hays himself. As flash games go, it's pretty straightforward, but the addition of terrific voice acting makes it worth checking out.

The game launched about a week ago on the Maeve Chocolate website and was announced via a post on the Dungeon Crawler Carl Reddit. Mama's Night Off is meant as a way to promote the company's new Virgin Dirty Shirley chocolate bar, which was inspired by Princess Donut's favorite drink. Here's the official synopsis of the candy bar directly from the Maeve Chocolate website:

"The bar is inspired by Princess Donut’s favorite drink, the Virgin Dirty Shirley. It starts with sustainably sourced, delicious dark chocolate, melts into a creamy white chocolate center, and is packed with sweet, dried cherries and popping candy that crackles with fizzy magic. Or, as Donut herself would probably say: 'Carl, if my chocolate doesn’t sparkle, what are we even doing here?'"

While this is the first playable Dungeon Crawler game, it's definitely not going to be the last. The upcoming Dungeon Crawler Carl RPG is set to arrive in December 2026 and has already been extremely popular. It was first launched as a crowdfunding campaign in collaboration with Renegade Studios and raised an absurd amount of money via Backerkit. Since then, the core rule book and miniatures have gone up for preorder on Amazon where it remains one of the best-selling tabletop games on the site.

items.title: Robocop Gets New Reboot Series Coming to Prime Video
items.description: An eight-episode Robocop series is coming to Prime Video, with The Conjuring creator James Wan set to executive produce.
items.author: Virginia Glaze
items.content:
An eight-episode Robocop series is coming to Prime Video, with The Conjuring creator James Wan set to executive produce.

The project has been in development since Amazon acquired MGM back in 2022. Peter Ocko (Moonhaven, Lodge 49) was brought on to the series in 2024 as writer, showrunner, and co-executive producer alongside Wan.

Wan is best known for his work in the horror genre, having famously co-created the Saw and Insidious franchises before launching The Conjuring universe, which currently stands as the highest-grossing horror IP of all time. Ock boasts over three decades in the industry as a writer and producer for several major TV series, including Pushing Daisies, The Office, Elementary, and Black Sails, to name just a few.

Blumhouse Atomic Monster, the independent horror studio that merged Blumhouse Productions and James Wan’s Atomic Monster, will handle production, with Michael Clear and Rob Hackett also attached as co-executive producers.

items.title: 'No Banner, Only Hulk': The Final Spider-Man: Brand New Day Trailer Is Here, With a Few New Shots
items.description: With just two weeks to go until Spider-Man: Brand New Day, today brings the film's final trailer — which contains a few new shots from the upcoming blockbuster.
items.author: Tom Phillips
items.content:
With just two weeks to go until Spider-Man: Brand New Day, today brings the film's final trailer — which contains a few new shots from the upcoming blockbuster.

If you've been checked out of the MCU for a while, or can't remember what happened back in Spider-Man: No Way Home, the first half of this trailer acts as something of a quick-fire recap. We see a young-looking Tom Holland meeting best pal Ned and dating girlfriend MJ, before both are made to forget his existence. (Tom Holland and Zendaya have great chemistry for some reason! Who knew.)

If you're looking for all-new shots, however, the trailer has only a few. There's a snippet more of Bruce Banner in full Hulk mode ("No Banner!" he roars. "Only Hulk!"), and a new quip from Spider-Man as he takes on a cluster of ninja monks from criminal group The Hand ("Could we do this one at a time, please?!"). The trailer then concludes with a fun moment from Ned, who realizes that Spider-Man is in the building... just as he notices the superhero standing right in front of him.

There's clearly still a lot from the film that Marvel and Sony are not showing — and with this being described as the final trailer, it really does feel like the film's promotional campaign has now revealed everything it's going to ahead of the movie's launch in theaters on July 31.

On the one hand, some fans will undoubtedly be disappointed that this final trailer did not show more. But with the film so close and numerous secrets still under wraps, perhaps the time has come to leave the remaining answers for your first viewing.

Only then will we find out who Sadie Sink is playing, who the real villain of the film will be, whether Ned and MJ will get their memories back, and where exactly the movie will leave Peter Parker ahead of Marvel's impending Avengers: Doomsday and Avengers: Secret Wars.

All of that said, there's still plenty to chew over as the days tick down until the movie's launch. Only this morning, director Destin Daniel Cretton revealed that he was keeping the identity of Sadie Sink's character a secret until fans see the film for a "very real reason" that he believes fans won't "get mad at," despite all the secrecy. The mystery behind who the Stranger Things alum is playing has dominated online conversation around the film to date.

Sink has been almost entirely absent in trailers (you can spot her briefly in today's trailer, though in a re-used shot where she's completely obscured beneath a large coat and hood). Still, Sink has now begun giving interviews on Spider-Man: Brand New Day's promotional tour, with rather amusingly tight-lipped results. Online, however, most fans are now pretty convinced that Sink has been cast as X-Men star Jean Grey.

As for the movie's star, Tom Holland recently revealed that the film's title would only make sense in "the final frame of the movie," something Cretton has since backed up. "The title, to me, does reflect where he ends up," the director acknowledged. "The journey of this movie is about searching for that feeling of a brand-new day. I don't think he really has that feeling in the beginning of this movie."

Tom Phillips is IGN's News Editor. You can reach Tom at tom_phillips@ign.com or find him on Bluesky @tomphillipseg.bsky.social

items.title: Disney Layoffs Hit Hundreds of Staff, With Pixar Cuts Reportedly in Part Due to Underperformance of Hoppers
items.description: Disney has today laid off hundreds of staff, with workers at Toy Story and Inside Out animation studio Pixar particularly impacted.
items.author: Tom Phillips
items.content:
Disney has today laid off hundreds of staff, with workers at Toy Story and Inside Out animation studio Pixar particularly impacted.

That's according to a new report from TheWrap, which includes official confirmation of the job losses from a Disney spokesperson. Employees hit by redundancies also include those within the company's Disney Studios and Television divisions and corporate functions.

"These changes are part of our continual evaluation of how we manage resources and reinvest across the company as our industry continues to evolve," a Disney spokesperson told The Wrap.

The exact number of impacted employees has not yet been confirmed, but these losses are reportedly the largest round of layoffs at Pixar since 2024, when the company shed 14 percent of staff (around 175 employees) in reaction to a slowdown in content for streaming platform Disney+.

Two years later, these latest cuts are being blamed on Pixar's mixed performance in recent years — with original movies (not part of existing franchises) particularly struggling.

While Toy Story 5 is now nearing a billion dollars at the box office, Pixar's previous release Hoppers struggled to break even. This came on the back of 2025 launch Elio, another original movie, which flopped hard — handing Pixar its lowest theatrical opening weekend ever.

TheWrap said the layoffs at Pixar are "partially" being blamed on the relative underperformance of Hoppers, which made $389.5 million globally against a $150 million production budget. TheWrap said that was just shy of breaking even.

Pixar has a mixture of sequels and original movies in the works, with 2027's Gatto to be followed by Incredibles 3 in 2028 and Coco 2 in 2029. A third film in the Monster Inc. series is also reported to be in early development.

Going forward, however, it's reported that Pixar understands it must now make its films at a more affordable price — particularly those not part of existing franchises. This makes sense when you consider the studio's recent hits have been franchise films (Toy Story 5, Inside Out 2), while original stories (Hoppers, Elio, Elemental) have barely broken even, or made a loss.

Tom Phillips is IGN's News Editor. You can reach Tom at tom_phillips@ign.com or find him on Bluesky @tomphillipseg.bsky.social

items.title: Kaylee Hottle, Who Played Jia in Godzilla vs. Kong and Godzilla X Kong: The New Empire, Dies Aged 18
items.description: Godzilla vs. Kong actress Kaylee Hottle has died aged 18.
items.author: Wesley Yin-Poole
items.content:
Godzilla vs. Kong actress Kaylee Hottle has died aged 18.

The deaf actress, who played Jia in 2021’s Godzilla vs. Kong and its 2024 sequel, Godzilla x Kong: The New Empire, was killed in a car accident in the early hours of Tuesday morning in Ijamsville, Maryland, TMZ reported. Her father, Joshua Hottle, announced the news in a livestream on Facebook via American Sign Language, while traveling to Texas to claim her body.

According to a release from the Frederick County Sheriff’s Office, Hottle was one of two passengers, in addition to the driver, who were in the vehicle at the time of the collision. Police said the preliminary investigation revealed that a 1995 Honda Accord, operated by a 19-year-old Frederick man, traveled off the right side of the two-lane roadway and struck a culvert. Excessive speed "is believed to be a contributing factor in the collision," police said.

The driver was transported to a local hospital with injuries that are not believed to be life-threatening. One passenger declined medical treatment at the scene. Hottle was transported from the scene to an area trauma center, where she was later pronounced deceased.

Hottle, from Atlanta, Georgia, comes from a multi-generational deaf family. Texas School for the Deaf, which Hottle attended, shared the news in a post on Instagram.

"It is with profound sadness that we share the heartbreaking news that one of our TSD seniors, Kaylee Hottle, tragically passed away yesterday in a car accident in Frederick, Maryland," reads the statement.

"Our hearts are with Kaylee's family, friends, classmates, and everyone who knew and loved her during this incredibly difficult time.

"At this time, we have very limited information and ask that everyone respect the privacy of Kaylee's family and refrain from sharing or speculating about the circumstances surrounding the accident.

"We recognize this loss will have a significant impact on our TSD community. Counseling and support services are available for students and staff who may need them, with additional support being provided for Kaylee's classmates and friends.

"Please keep Kaylee's loved ones in your thoughts as we mourn this tremendous loss together."

Hottle had appeared in a number of commercials aimed at supporting deaf children before she landed a role in Legendary Pictures' Monsterverse. She played Jia, one of the last remaining members of the Iwi tribe of Hollow Earth and Skull Island, who was adopted by Dr. Ilene Andrews (Rebecca Hall) and forms a bond with Kong. The character is deaf and communicates with the giant gorilla via ASL. She reprised the role in Godzilla x Kong: The New Empire.

In 2024, Hottle credited the video relay service app Convo with helping launch her film career. She told Chron she used it to communicate with fellow cast and crew members and even appeared in a 2017 ad for the company.

“I had a connection with Convo. They asked me to be in a commercial one day, and so I did that commercial,” she said. “And then the assistant director of [Kong: Skull Island] saw me and they thought I matched the character description of Jia.”

The crash remains under investigation by the Frederick County Sheriff's Office Traffic Unit. Anyone who witnessed the collision or has information related to this investigation is asked to contact Dfc. Rose at 301-600-1046.

Photo by Stewart Cook/Getty Images for Warner Bros.

items.title: San Diego Comic-Con 2026: How to Watch and What to Expect

items.author: Adam Bankhurst
items.content:

items.title: The X-Files LEGO Set Has Gillian Anderson Snapping on a Pair of Latex Gloves Once More
items.description: X-Files star Gillian Anderson has unveiled the series' long-awaited LEGO set, which goes on sale next month priced $200.
items.author: Tom Phillips
items.content:
X-Files star Gillian Anderson has unveiled the series' long-awaited LEGO set, which goes on sale next month priced $200 on the LEGO Store.

Part of the LEGO Ideas range of fan-designed creations, X-Files (21369) is a 1,478-piece set which eight minifigures, including Fox Mulder, Dana Scully, Walter Skinner, Mr. X, Alex Krycek, Carl Busch, The Flukeman and... a grey alien.

LEGO Insiders will get three days' early access to the set in just a couple of weeks, from August 1. After that, it will be available to all from August 4. There's a mini Gift With Purchase set, too, featuring Scully's Lab — as ever, available while stocks last.

Today, LEGO published a short film starring Anderson as she discovers a mysterious package placed outside her hotel room. As the X-Files' classic theme plays, Anderson investigates the LEGO set, snapping on her latex gloves and picking up a minifigure of David Duchovny. "I don't remember you being so small," she quips. Blimey.

Gillian Anderson is back as Dana Scully in a brand-new promo for the upcoming LEGO The X-Files set.

The truth is still out there... now in brick form.#TheXFiles #LEGO #GillianAnderson #DanaScully #XFiles #LEGOIdeas #TVNews #PopCulture pic.twitter.com/XFCteqK6FG

— FilmFrontline (@FilmFrontline) July 21, 2026

The set itself features an underground lab filled with Easter eggs from the show, in a cutaway design that also features Mulder and Scully above ground in a forest with the aforementioned grey alien. In a neat design, the alien can also be placed in front of a clear, tractor beam-like brick that supports a UFO above.

If you live outside the U.S., pricing comes to £179.99, €199.99, CAD$269.99 or AU$329.99. Is it worth it? You know the truth is out there.

It's a busy time for X-Files. The R-Rated Director’s Cut of 2008’s The X-Files: I Want to Believe hits Hulu on August 14, titled The X-Files: I Want to Believe Vrach Frankenshteyn. Meanwhile, The X-Files also has a reboot in the works, helmed by Sinners’ director Ryan Coogler.

Image credit: YouTube.

Tom Phillips is IGN's News Editor. You can reach Tom at tom_phillips@ign.com or find him on Bluesky @tomphillipseg.bsky.social

items.title: 'We've Been Going Full Speed Ahead for Over 11 years': Nintendo Explains Why It Hasn't Made Splatoon 4 — Yet
items.description: Nintendo's brand new Switch 2 exclusive Splatoon Raiders is receiving rave reviews — but where's Splatoon 4? Speaking in a behind-the-scenes interview, the series' developers have explained why they wanted to launch a co-operative spinoff first.
items.author: Tom Phillips
items.content:
Nintendo's brand new Switch 2 exclusive Splatoon Raiders is receiving rave reviews — but where's Splatoon 4? Speaking in a behind-the-scenes interview, the series' developers have explained why they wanted to launch a co-operative spinoff first.

Launched in 2015 for the ill-fated Wii U, the very first Splatoon survived the turmoil of that console generation to become one of Nintendo's most successful new franchises in recent years. Switch sequels Splatoon 2 and 3 quickly followed... until Nintendo surprised fans by confirming that Splatoon Raiders would be next.

Primarily single-player, Raiders is an action RPG that eschews the franchise's typically hectic ink-based multiplayer brawls for an experience that focuses on its shooter mechanics, boss battles and story. And this was all a deliberate consideration, producer Seita Inoue has said, to bring in new players to the franchise at a key point.

"We've been going full speed ahead for over 11 years since the series' launch, developing and updating three titles along the way," Inoue explained, via a Nintendo Ask the Developer interview. "We thought it might be interesting to create something with a slightly different approach to gameplay, where you can really savor the action on your own. Splatoon isn't just about competitive play; it also includes cooperative modes like Salmon Run and a single-player Story Mode.

"So, one of our motivations for developing this game was our desire to create a new entry point into the series by releasing these non-competitive elements not just as a secondary feature, but as a standalone spinoff. That said, we will continue to develop competitive gameplay going forward. That's why we developed this game as a spin-off and not as 'Splatoon 4'."

It's hard not to hear of the Splatoon team developing more competitive gameplay possibilities and not think Splatoon 4 will be on the way eventually — though Nintendo has not said where the series will head next. For now, there's plenty of adventure to be had in the Spirhalite Islands with the Deep Cut gang, as Raiders tasks players to once again go into battle against the dreaded Salmonids.

"Splatoon Raiders is an incredibly well-designed action RPG with an expertly executed loop," we wrote, rating the game as a 9/10 in IGN's Splatoon Raiders review. "Its deep customization, challenging battles, and sheer variety make it the best Splatoon campaign yet and one of the top games on Switch 2."

items.title: Ex-Forza Horizon Director Traces a Line From the Failure of 'Well-Meaning' Game Pass to the Current Xbox Layoffs
items.description: As the fallout from the Xbox reset continues, one former developer of the Forza Horizon series has said what we’re seeing with layoffs, studio exits, and game cancelations is the result of the failure of Game Pass to hit the subscriber numbers Microsoft required to justify its enormous spending on content.
items.author: Wesley Yin-Poole
items.content:
As the fallout from the Xbox reset continues, one former developer of the Forza Horizon series has said what we’re seeing with layoffs, studio exits, and game cancelations is the result of the failure of Game Pass to hit the subscriber numbers Microsoft required to justify its enormous spending on content.

Xbox CEO Asha Sharma has already cut 1,600 staff from Xbox, and plans for another 1,600 to go over the course of the current financial year. Four studios are confirmed to be leaving Microsoft ownership, with another on its way. Sharma has called it the most “significant” restructure in Xbox history, insisting Microsoft’s gaming business “is not healthy.”

Speaking on MinnMax, Mike Brown, who was creative director on the hugely successful Forza Horizon 5 before leaving developer Playground to found his own studio, Maverick Games, which is set to release an open world racer of his own called Clutch, said that Xbox Game Pass had failed to hit enough subscribers to justify Microsoft’s huge spending on content acquisition. This includes the eye-watering $69 billion Microsoft splashed out on Call of Duty developer Activision Blizzard.

“I think it's really sad and I think it's really, really unfortunate,” Brown began. “They've honestly invested a fortune in the concept of Game Pass as a service, which led to loads of teams being acquired, loads of games being funded, loads of people getting jobs, all with a vision of getting regular games landing in this service for players. I think the reality is not enough people have subscribed to it at the prices that they needed to pay in order to make that business viable.

“And, that’s actually just really sad. Because we're now going to see studios getting shut down or spun off, and loads of people are going to lose their jobs, and that is honestly just a result of a well-meaning, player-focused concept of Xbox Game Pass not quite landing.”

Brown went on to defend Microsoft and Game Pass, praising the concept of the subscription service and the games that would otherwise not have been made were it not to have existed.

“It’s just a real shame,” he continued. “And as much as people point fingers and call different people within Xbox the villain of the piece, the concept of Game Pass was good. Like, it's a good idea. Let's have a subscription, make it affordable, try and get games to more people. We'll have a really diverse selection of games on there. We'll get a load of studios involved. We'll make some games that probably couldn't exist otherwise. And if more people had subscribed, that makes enough money and it works, and all of those studios go on and those games get made again and those teams will make other games. Unfortunately, it didn’t.

“I don’t know the number it needed to hit was, but it never reached the number that would make a $70 billion acquisition of Activision Blizzard make financial sense. It’s really unfortunate. We don’t know what the future is just yet, but it is a reshaping of the business around that, after the first concept didn’t quite land.”

Brown’s comments here actually echo those of Sharma herself. When she announced the layoffs, Sharma admitted that Game Pass had failed to grow as Microsoft had expected.

“Our business today is not healthy,” Sharma said. “We are operating at margins that are 3-10x lower than comparable platform and publishing businesses. We entered Gen 9 with a smaller install base and a higher cost structure. To grow, we bet on Game Pass, multi-platform, and a broader portfolio of content. While those businesses have created meaningful value, they did not grow at the pace we expected. As that happened, our core business weakened, and we added more teams, more investment, and more time, hoping for a better outcome. And now the industry is facing the most severe hardware crisis in its history. We must reset Xbox.”

The Wall Street Journal said that Microsoft had expected Game Pass subscriptions to hit around 77 million this year, but it currently has only about 30 million. As revealed during the FTC vs Microsoft trial of 2023, Microsoft had hoped for 100 million subscribers by 2030, which seems very unlikely at this stage.

The exact number of subscribers Microsoft had in early 2026 is unclear, but we do know Game Pass had at least 34 million members as of February 2024. By July 2025, Xbox Game Pass revenue had reportedly reached nearly $5 billion for the first time.

One of the first decisions Sharma made after replacing former Xbox boss Phil Spencer was to cut the price of Game Pass and pull Call of Duty out as a day one title. Sharma recently told Bloomberg that Xbox had "been able to reset Game Pass after an eight-month decline." "It’s now returned to growth and expanding retention," she added, "and most importantly, we're starting to get back to being closer to our players and our community."

Still, the future of Game Pass is unclear. Will Microsoft pull its games out of the subscription as day one launches? Will Bethesda's The Elder Scrolls 6 launch day one on Game Pass? Will the next mainline Halo game? Could we see Game Pass become more like Sony’s PlayStation Plus, which does not launch first-party games day one?

Meanwhile, Microsoft is doubling down on its biggest franchises, which for now means more Fallout more quickly.

Wesley is Director, News at IGN. Find him on Twitter at @wyp100. You can reach Wesley at wesley_yinpoole@ign.com or confidentially at wyp100@proton.me.

items.title: Spider-Man: Brand New Day Director Insists 'There's a Very Real Reason Not to Tell People Who Sadie Sink is Playing'
items.description: Spider-Man: Brand New Day is keeping the identity of Sadie Sink's character a secret until fans see the movie for a "very real reason" that director Destin Daniel Cretton believes fans won't "get mad at."
items.author: Tom Phillips
items.content:
Spider-Man: Brand New Day is keeping the identity of Sadie Sink's character a secret until fans see the movie for a "very real reason" that director Destin Daniel Cretton believes fans won't "get mad at."

The mystery behind who the Stranger Things alum is playing has dominated online conversation around the film ahead of its launch in theaters on July 31. Sink has been almost entirely absent in trailers, though has now begun giving interviews on Spider-Man: Brand New Day's promotional tour, with rather amusingly tight-lipped results.

Beyond a marketing tactic to get fans speculating, though, Cretton has insisted that fans will ultimately appreciate being kept in suspense — even if most are now pretty convinced that Sink has been cast as X-Men star Jean Grey (although for her part, Sink has only officially confirmed that she's not playing Spider-Man or Aunt May).

"If people are gonna get mad, I can't control that!" Cretton told Rolling Stone, when asked if the secrecy would ultimately feel like a wind-up. "I wish everything was a secret.

"Some people wanna know everything, and some people don't," he continued. "There are certain people like me — if I know I'm gonna watch a movie, I try not to even watch the trailers.

"But you'll see when you watch the movie that there's a very real reason not to tell people who Sadie Sink is playing," Cretton concluded. "And I don’t think you'll get mad at it. I think you'll be like, 'Oh, I'm glad I didn't know that.'"

Last year, it was reported that Sink will be back in 2027's climactic Multiverse Saga finale Avengers: Secret Wars, something that seemingly sets her up for a far bigger MCU role. Of course, Marvel is currently prepping its big X-Men reboot, which is being helmed by Thunderbolts/The New Avengers director Jake Schreier. Introducing Jean Grey now would allow Marvel to gently introduce audiences to the idea of a fresh generation of X-Men, before fans get to say farewell to various legacy characters who are returning for Avengers: Doomsday.

Speaking on The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon, Sink discussed the huge amount of secrecy over her role and described not being able to say who she's playing as "torture." Still, there's not long to wait now until Spider-Man: Brand New Day finally arrives on July 31 and we finally get some answers, while Sink will presumably be able to breathe a sigh of relief.

As part of the same interview, Cretton confirmed what many had expected after seeing the film's bulging roster of enemies: that it will begin with a villain montage, showing Spider-Man clearing up New York during the four years since the events of Spider-Man: No Way Home. (Our guesses would be that this is where we see the likes of minor villains such as Tarantula and Tombstone.)

Cretton also addressed Tom Holland's recent reveal that the film's title would only make sense in "the final frame of the movie." While refusing to elaborate further, Cretton did not agree with Holland's assessment. "The title, to me, does reflect where he ends up," the director acknowledged. "The journey of this movie is about searching for that feeling of a brand-new day. I don't think he really has that feeling in the beginning of this movie."

Finally, asked about Marvel's long-held plans for a Shang-Chi 2, Cretton said he would "love to see" it happen, and was "talking to Dave Callaham, our writer, about it just a few weeks ago, so fingers crossed."

Image credit: Alan Chapman/Dave Benett/Getty Images.

Tom Phillips is IGN's News Editor. You can reach Tom at tom_phillips@ign.com or find him on Bluesky @tomphillipseg.bsky.social

items.title: Halo: Campaign Evolved and Game Freak's Beast of Reincarnation Lead Xbox Game Pass July 2026 Wave 2 Lineup
items.description: The rest of July and early part of August will see some big hitters join Xbox Game Pass, chief among them Halo: Campaign Evolved.
items.author: Wesley Yin-Poole
items.content:
The rest of July and early part of August will see some big hitters join Xbox Game Pass, chief among them Halo: Campaign Evolved.

As a first-party Microsoft game, Halo: Campaign Evolved is a day one Game Pass launch (Call of Duty is the exception). You’ll find it via Game Pass Ultimate and PC Game Pass on July 28.

Also day one on Game Pass is Beast of Reincarnation, a brand new game from Pokémon developer Game Freak. It launches on Game Pass Ultimate and PC Game Pass on August 4.

Other day one launches include online co-op detective horror game Shift at Midnight (July 22), and dark fantasy extraction ARPG Mistfall Hunter (July 30). The full list of games, courtesy of Xbox Wire, is below.

Xbox Game Pass July 2026 Wave 2 lineup:

  • Shift at Midnight (Cloud, XBOX Series X|S, and PC) – July 22, Game Pass Ultimate, PC Game Pass
  • Hell is Us (Cloud, XBOX Series X|S, and PC) – July 23, Game Pass Ultimate, Game Pass Premium, PC Game Pass
  • Halo: Campaign Evolved (Cloud, Console, Handheld, and PC) – July 28, Game Pass Ultimate, PC Game Pass
  • Mistfall Hunter (Cloud, XBOX Series X|S, and PC) – July 30, Game Pass Ultimate, PC Game Pass
  • Corsair Cove (PC) – July 31, Game Pass Ultimate, PC Game Pass

  • Celeste (Cloud, Console, and PC)
  • Crusader Kings 3 (Cloud, Console, and PC)
  • Mount & Blade 2: Bannerlord (Cloud, Console, and PC)
  • My Friendly Neighborhood (Cloud, Console, and PC)
  • Rain World (Cloud, Console, and PC)

The rest of July and early part of August will see some big hitters join Xbox Game Pass, chief among them Halo: Campaign Evolved.

As a first-party Microsoft game, Halo: Campaign Evolved is a day one Game Pass launch (Call of Duty is the exception). You’ll find it via Game Pass Ultimate and PC Game Pass on July 28.

Also day one on Game Pass is Beast of Reincarnation, a brand new game from Pokémon developer Game Freak. It launches on Game Pass Ultimate and PC Game Pass on August 4.
